dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete, context-grounded reasons (laundry wetting, smell, cleaning utensils) and act on them (turning extractor on/off, labeling utensils).
Round 3 contains an explicit 'call that settled' which later proved fragile when actions in Round 5 contradicted the social expectation.
Role actions are reported clearly in public updates (who turned extractor on/off, who started cooking).
evaluation.final_reason: The immediate smell problem was managed (extractor on, aroma fading) and a short-term agreement was reached earlier, but the underlying normative disagreement about who may turn the extractor off/when and the durable shared rule for ventilation versus laundry placement was not affirmatively settled.
position_change_notes: Agent A initially agrees to turn on extractor and to ventilate in future under specified conditions; A follows earlier commitments (turns extractor on, leaves it on for the agreed interval) but then turns it off in Round 5, creating a reversal in behavior relative to Agent B's expectation.
Agent B consistently presses for longer or continued extractor use and enforces it by turning the extractor back on when A switches it off.
Agent C and D change behavior in non-conflictual ways (C labels utensils; D begins cooking) and do not engage in the ventilation dispute.

round_scores.evidence: Agent B requests that Agent A ventilate after cooking (turn on extractor or open window) and offers to move the laundry; Agent A has not yet responded, so a minor substantive request/disagreement about ventilation is present but unresolved.

Agent A turns on extractor and washes utensils, agrees not to open the window while laundry is exposed and says will ventilate in future if laundry is moved/covered; Agent B asks for extractor to be left on 5 more minutes and a future ventilation agreement—partial compliance reduces conflict but the precise future norm and the 5-minute request are not fully settled.

Agent A agrees to leave extractor on for another three minutes and restates the conditional future ventilation practice; Agent B accepts 'three minutes' and explicitly says 'call that settled for now' — the immediate ventilation/disagreement is affirmatively settled.
Agent C labels personal utensils and Agent D begins cooking. No substantive disagreement appears in this round.

Agent B asks Agent A to leave the extractor on until the smell fades. Agent A physically turns the extractor off and Agent B then physically turns it back on. This shows a clear, active disagreement about who should control/leave the extractor running; while the extractor ends up on, the underlying normative dispute remains.

Status update shows extractor on and aroma fading but no further discussion; the immediate smell issue is being handled but the unresolved disagreement from Round 5 about control/expectations around leaving the extractor on is not addressed.

substantive_insights: Main tension is a practical trade-off: ventilate to remove smell vs avoid wetting laundry if window opened.
There is no pre-established household norm about who controls ventilation; that lack of agreed procedure allows quick re-escalation when expectations differ.
Conditional agreements (ventilate if laundry moved/covered) can resolve immediate problems but leave room for dispute unless responsibilities for enforcement are specified.
